title: Songs of the Watering Eye
logline: At a tavern leaning over a well that folds every face it has held, the Genie prices wishes for locals — and Boof's small asks come back unpriceable.
epigraph: The well keeps every face; the tavern keeps every round. Between them, all debts are known.
description: Chapter 8 of Lore.Land: Songs of the Watering Eye. A tavern leans over a well that folds every face it has held. The Off-Season Genie runs his negotiation game, pricing wishes for locals, and finds that ordinary desires resist his machinery more than empires do. The water names the debt in the egg's heat.

content.text: The Watering Eye was a well before it was a witness, and a witness long before anyone built a tavern leaning over it like a drinker over a confession. Boof came in under the sagging floorboards and set her front paws on the mossy coping. The water below was black and perfectly still, and it did not show her own face first. It showed her an older one — a woman mid-wish, mouth open on a want she had never said aloud — and under that face, folded like pressed linen going down into the dark, every other face the well had ever held. From the barrel-head behind her came the

children.text: , brisk as a market morning: "I can make you famous by Tuesday, or respected by November. Fame is cheap — reality already leans that way for loud people. Respect requires corrections. Choose."

content.text: A face said into deep water is not stolen; it is folded, and it stays the property of whoever wore it. The well kept the faces the way an honest ledger keeps a debt: patiently, and without letting anyone else spend them.

content.text: All night the Genie dealt in wants. Name one, hear the price, pay or fold. An empire? Quite manageable; the world was forever tipping toward a throne. Supper everyone agreed on? He counted the company twice and quoted three coincidences and a fortnight of Thursdays. At the bar, the regular raised his glass. “Six violations of the natural order,” the Genie told him. “Lager,” said the regular. The Genie wrote it down. After a moment, he underlined it.

content.text: Eighth honk: the tavern game, sampled and returned — small wants priced dear, because they are the ones the world was not already planning to grant.
He sat the trapdoor's edge with his boots over the dark, tapping the game's rhythm on the iron ring, taking the tavern's off-key song and handing it back on-key, with interest.

sections.figcaption: The Watering Eye: the tavern names the wants; the water names the debts.

content.text: Near closing, he tried Boof again. “Anything. Name it.” She thought of the furrow, the warmth, a trail with something real at its end. His needle swung beyond the numbers and came back blank. He reset it. She tried again. Same small click, same empty dial. Boof lowered the egg onto the wet stone around the well. Heat spread under her paws, through the coping, down.

The folded faces stirred. One by one they turned toward the warmth the way the berries once had, and the water said, in the plain way water says things, what every face down there had in common: each one owed a coincidence to a stranger, and the egg — an unspent wish — was the debt still standing warm above the fold. The well could not price it either. It only named it, and kept the account open. Boof leaned over the rim without touching the water. Some faces were clear enough to count the lines around a mouth; others drifted beneath reflections of the tavern windows. A laugh came through the floorboards overhead, and for a moment she could not tell whether one of the faces had laughed too. She moved the egg closer. Ripples reached the far wall and came back through the reflected light. The Genie stood beside her with his instruments shut. She was glad he had stopped asking her to name it.

content.text: "What did I win?" Boof wondered, taking the egg back into her sling. The Genie had priced fame, thrones, and six lagers, and had folded on her — the only player at the table whose want his game could not hold. Behind her the regular raised one finger at the dark, on principle.

She climbed toward the roofs with the well's answer warming her ribs. The egg was a debt. The faces below had turned toward it together, though no voice had called them. Above the ridge, eight old notes hung in the dark. She listened for the missing one and felt it humming against her chest.

loreItems.description: The Watering Eye folds a face without stealing it — a want said into deep water still belongs to its wanter.
Ordinary desires resist wish fulfillment more than spectacular ones: thrones are cheap, supper agreements are advanced karmic problems.
The water names the debt in the egg's heat: an unspent wish standing warm above the fold, owing a coincidence to a stranger.
